quickAnswer: In 2026, Turkish Citizenship by Investment via real estate requires purchasing eligible property worth at least USD 400,000 with a three-year non-resale annotation recorded on the TAPU title deed. Applicants must convert funds through a Turkish bank for a DAB certificate, pass SPK-licensed valuation checks, and allow 8 to 12 months from TAPU transfer to passport issuance.
category: Real Estate, Investment, Citizenship & Relocation (ITO Advisory)

body.text: What are the current $400,000 minimum valuation and 3-year hold rules?

Under Article 12 of Turkish Citizenship Law No. 5901 and Presidential regulations, foreign investors qualify by acquiring real estate worth at least USD 400,000 (or equivalent foreign currency) and registering a three-year no-sale restriction (şerh) at the Land Registry. Both the declared TAPU price, the SPK-licensed appraisal, and bank payment receipts must independently meet or exceed USD 400,000.

As outlined by [Invest in Türkiye](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/investmentguide/pages/acquiring-property-and-citizenship.aspx) and the [Directorate General of Population and Citizenship Affairs (NVI)](https://www.nvi.gov.tr/sss-vatandaslik-hizmetleri), the property may be one unit or multiple qualifying units totaling USD 400,000, provided each carries the three-year commitment and has not previously been used for another citizenship application. Following September 2026 regulatory updates, any Capital Markets Board (SPK)-authorized valuation company connected to TADEBİS may prepare the appraisal report, with Title Deed Conformity (TTB) validity set at 12 months ([FT Portföy 2026 Update](https://ftportfoy.com/turkish-citizenship-property-valuation-rule-change-2026.html)).
How does the DAB (Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate) work through a Turkish bank?

Before the Land Registry transfers ownership, the buyer must sell the USD 400,000+ purchase amount in foreign currency (USD, EUR, or GBP) to a Turkish bank, which routes it to the Central Bank (TCMB). The bank then issues a Foreign Exchange Purchase Certificate (Döviz Alım Belgesi, DAB) locking the official TRY equivalent.

Per [2026 DAB compliance guidance](https://www.garsconsulting.com/tr/blog/doviz-alim-belgesi-dab-turkey-guide-2026) and [Legal 500 Türkiye 2026](https://www.legal500.com/intelligence/turkey/real-estate-and-construction/real-estate-investment-in-t%C3%BCrkiye-2026), exchange offices (döviz büroları) are strictly invalid for DAB issuance. The DAB document must list the buyer's full passport name, passport number, Turkish tax number, exact province/district/parcel (ada/parsel) details, and the explicit purpose of real estate acquisition for Turkish citizenship, matching the bank-to-bank Turkish Lira wire sent directly to the seller.
How long does the full citizenship application take from TAPU to passport?

In 2026, a clean real estate citizenship file typically takes 8 to 12 months from TAPU registration to final Presidential approval and passport issuance, though authorities do not guarantee fixed timelines. Processing moves sequentially through the Certificate of Eligibility, the Article 31/1(j) investor residence permit, and multi-agency security and archive reviews managed by NVI.

body.text: Which common valuation or developer pitfalls cause rejections?

Inflated appraisals, cash side-agreements, and incomplete foreign-currency trails are the leading causes of citizenship refusals and retroactive revocations in 2026. By August 2026, Turkish authorities had cancelled or withdrawn citizenship decisions for over 5,300 investors and family members tied to irregular or fraudulent valuation reports, underscoring strict post-approval audits ([Turchina Group 2026 Review](https://www.turchinagroup.com/en/blog/turkish-citizenship-revocations-clean-investment-file)).

items: Verify that the independent SPK appraisal reflects true local comparable sales—never accept a developer's offer to "boost" a USD 250,000 unit to USD 400,000.

Confirm the seller is a Turkish citizen or Turkish-owned entity and that the property was not previously owned by a foreign national within the restricted statutory window or used for prior citizenship.
Wire 100% of the purchase funds from the buyer's own bank account through a Turkish bank with full DAB documentation—never pay cash or route funds through unlicensed intermediaries.
Check for existing mortgages, tax liens, or missing İskan occupancy certificates before signing any preliminary contract.
Retain an independent Turkish real estate and immigration attorney who has zero financial relationship with the seller or developer.

faq.q: Does the $400,000 real estate investment cover my spouse and children?
faq.a: Yes. Under Law No. 5901, the main investor's spouse and dependent children under age 18 can be included in the same citizenship application at no extra property investment threshold.

faq.q: Can I buy two apartments totaling $400,000 instead of one property?
faq.a: Yes. Multiple qualifying properties can be combined to reach USD 400,000, provided all SPK valuations, DAB certificates, bank transfers, and three-year no-sale annotations are properly aligned.

faq.q: Can I rent out the property during the 3-year holding period?
faq.a: Yes. The three-year annotation (şerh) restricts selling or transferring ownership, not leasing the property for rental income—subject to local short-term or long-term rental tax rules verified by a licensed accountant.

faq.q: What happens if the Turkish Lira fluctuates after my DAB is issued?
faq.a: The DAB locks the official USD equivalent on the exact date the Turkish bank converts your foreign currency via the Central Bank. Keeping a modest USD buffer (e.g., USD 405,000–410,000) protects against minor intraday conversion spreads.

faq.q: Do I have to live in Türkiye or pass a Turkish language test?
faq.a: No. Exceptional citizenship by investment does not impose a minimum physical residency requirement or Turkish language exam, though applicants must attend biometrics either in Türkiye or at a Turkish diplomatic mission abroad.
